evals.prompt: I want to start a fresh LLM wiki. I just watched Karpathy's 'Intro to Large Language Models' talk — can you ingest the key concepts from it? Here are the main topics he covered: what LLMs are (next token prediction on internet text), how training works (pretraining vs fine-tuning), emergent capabilities at scale, tool use and system prompts, security risks (jailbreaks, prompt injection), and the future of LLM OS. Set up the wiki structure and create the initial pages.
evals.expected_output: Should create wiki directory structure (SCHEMA.md, index.md, log.md), save raw source, create entity/concept/source pages with proper frontmatter and wikilinks, and pass validation

assertions.text: index.md exists and lists all created pages
Source page created for the talk
All pages have YAML frontmatter with required fields
Each page has at least 2 outbound wikilinks

evals.prompt: I have an existing LLM wiki with a few pages about transformers and attention. Now I want to add this article about Flash Attention: 'Flash Attention by Tri Dao introduces an IO-aware exact attention algorithm that reduces memory from O(N^2) to O(N) by tiling the computation and avoiding materializing the full attention matrix. It achieves 2-4x wall-clock speedup over standard attention in PyTorch. FlashAttention-2 further improves this with better work partitioning across GPU thread blocks. Key insight: the bottleneck in attention is memory bandwidth, not FLOPs.' Add this to the wiki and make sure it connects to existing pages about attention and transformers.
evals.expected_output: Should read existing wiki state (session start protocol), create source page for the article, create/update concept pages for Flash Attention and related topics, update index and log, and run validation

assertions.text: Session start protocol followed (read SCHEMA, index, log)
Source page created for Flash Attention article
Concept page created for Flash Attention
Existing attention/transformer pages updated with links to Flash Attention

evals.prompt: Run a quality check on my LLM wiki. I think there might be some broken links and pages that are missing proper metadata. Give me a full report and fix any issues you find.
evals.expected_output: Should run the Lint operation: execute validate-wiki.ps1, report all issues across 8 dimensions, fix broken links and missing frontmatter, and re-run until score >= 9.0
